t:
(a) In General.—Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the United States is not required to perform, or to reimburse the District of Columbia for the cost of performing, any of the following services:
        (1) Repairs or renovations pursuant to section 4(f) of the Saint Elizabeths Hospital and District of Columbia Mental Health Services Act (24 U.S.C. 225b(f); sec. 44–903(f), D.C. Official Code). 
        (2) Preservation, maintenance, or repairs pursuant to a use permit executed on September 30, 1987, under which the United States (acting through the Secretary of Health and Human Services) granted permission to the District of Columbia to use and occupy portions of the Saint Elizabeths Hospital property known as the “West Campus”. 
        (3) Mental health diagnostic and treatment services for referrals as described in section 9(b) of the Saint Elizabeths Hospital and District of Columbia Mental Health Services Act (24 U.S.C. 225g(b); sec. 44–908(b), D.C. Official Code), but only with respect to services provided on or before the date of the enactment of this Act.  
    (b) Effect on Pending Claims.—Any claim of the District of Columbia against the United States for the failure to perform, 
or to reimburse the District of Columbia for the cost of performing, any service described in subsection (a) which is pending as of the date of the enactment of this Act shall be extinguished and terminated.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the references to the District of Columbia (a non-federal government) and to its claims against the United States signal outside-party involvement or a right to sue. In fact the section relieves the United States of certain obligations and extinguishes pending claims, which removes litigation rights rather than granting them. It provides no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, or advisory body involving outside parties in a federal decision.
fable.s:
Any claim of the District of Columbia against the United States for the failure to perform, 
or to reimburse the District of Columbia for the cost of performing, any service described in subsection (a) which is pending as of the date of the enactment of this Act shall be extinguished and terminated.

opus.w: The section says the United States does not have to perform or pay for certain services, and it ends DC's pending claims against the United States. Ending a right to sue is the opposite of granting one, so the litigation part of the definition does not apply. No consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or rulemaking brings outside parties into a federal decision.
opus.s:
Any claim of the District of Columbia against the United States for the failure to perform, 
or to reimburse the District of Columbia for the cost of performing, any service described in subsection (a) which is pending as of the date of the enactment of this Act shall be extinguished and terminated.
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes": the District of Columbia is outside the federal government, and the section talks about its "claim ... against the United States." That fails because the section takes away DC's claims instead of giving it a right to sue. Nothing else in the section involves outside parties in a federal decision. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or rulemaking.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the financial obligations of the federal government toward the District of Columbia, specifically stating that the US is not required to perform or reimburse for certain services. It does not require the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from the District of Columbia or any other outside party before making a decision. The extinguishment of claims is a legislative determination, not a participatory process involving outside parties in the decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: the United States is not required to perform, or to reimburse the District of Columbia for the cost of performing, any of the following services
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the District of Columbia is an outside entity, any interaction with it constitutes participation. However, this section merely defines financial liabilities and extinguishes claims; it does not require the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from the District of Columbia before making a decision. The decision (to not pay) is made by statute, not through a participatory process.
